questions: Should the list include the starting number n if it is odd, or only odd numbers encountered after applying the rule?
Is the input n guaranteed to be a positive integer, or should the function handle zero, negative integers, or non-integer inputs?
Should the list include duplicates if an odd number appears multiple times in the sequence?
Is the sequence defined to stop when reaching 1, or continue indefinitely (e.g., 1 -> 4 -> 2 -> 1 ...)?
Should the output list be sorted in ascending order as per the clarification, or is any sorted order acceptable?
If n is 1, should the output be [1] or an empty list?
Are floating-point numbers allowed in the sequence (e.g., from division), and should they be converted to integers for oddness check?
Should the function return an empty list if there are no odd numbers in the sequence (e.g., for even n that produce only even numbers until 1)?
